papers.title_en: PerturbJEPA: Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning of Cellular Perturbation Responses
papers.authors: Jiangshuan Pang, Youzhe He, Yiting Deng, Wangyang Tang, Huinan Xu, Qi Lu, Shiping Liu, Zhenkun Zhuang
papers.evidence: 通过联合嵌入学习预测细胞扰动响应
papers.tldr: 细胞扰动响应预测需在保留背景差异的同时保留处理效应，否则联合嵌入模型会出现干预对比坍缩。PerturbJEPA将处理组与对照组平均表达差编码为效应向量，并对齐潜在质心位移、正则化效应向量以保留群体对间变异。在Tahoe-100M的3592个留出组合查询上，其宏平均联合药物-剂量Recall@1达91.46%，较STATE高3.40个百分点。该工作为无需细胞配对或表达重建的扰动响应匹配提供了新框架。
papers.abstract_en: Identifying the drug and dose that produced a cellular response requires preserving treatment effects within each cellular background. A joint-embedding predictor can match its targets while ignoring the intervention if its encoder preserves differences across backgrounds but erases differences between treated and control populations within each one. We call this failure interventional contrast collapse. PerturbJEPA encodes the difference in mean gene expression between treated and control populations as an effect vector. It aligns the displacement between their latent centroids with this vector and regularizes the vectors to preserve variation across population pairs. We show that the measured displacements cannot all coincide within a batch when effect-vector variation exceeds the root-mean-square alignment error. Trained with separate drug and dose ranking objectives, the model predicts candidate responses from a common control population and matches them to the observed response without cell pairing or expression reconstruction. We evaluate 3,592 Tahoe-100M queries on held-out combinations of known interventions and cellular backgrounds, each with over 700 drug-dose candidates in a fixed, background-specific catalog. PerturbJEPA achieves 91.46% macro joint drug-dose Recall@1, exceeding STATE by 3.40 percentage points (95% drug-cluster bootstrap interval of 1.72 to 5.07 points). Controlled diagnostics show that treatment-control differences can shrink even when representations remain globally dispersed. With the drug ranking objective fixed, adding effect-vector regularization to alignment raises joint Recall@1 from 18.57% to 87.47%.

papers.title_en: PerturbBridge: Conditional Latent Schr dinger Bridge for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
papers.authors: Liu, Z., Jiang, C., Yang, C., Wang, X., Liu, X.
papers.evidence: 用条件潜空间薛定谔桥进行单细胞扰动响应预测
papers.tldr: 单细胞扰动预测需从非配对对照与扰动群体推断未见干预的转录响应，而高维稀疏表达使直接学习桥动态困难。PerturbBridge 用响应锚定自编码器构建保留主扰动响应方向的潜空间，并以可处理的薛定谔桥近似建模条件随机传输。其扰动诱导桥 Transformer 通过扰动与时间槽引导潜坐标交互来估计漂移。在 Norman、Sci-Plex3 与 Replogle RPE1 上，差异表达方向恢复和扰动效应相关性领先，基因表达预测具竞争力。
papers.abstract_en: \textbf{Motivation:}Single-cell perturbation prediction seeks to recover transcriptional responses to unseen interventions from unpaired control and perturbed populations. The Schr\"odinger Bridge provides a principled framework for modeling these transitions as stochastic transport, but learning bridge dynamics directly from high-dimensional, sparse gene-expression profiles remains challenging. \textbf{Results:} We present PerturbBridge, a conditional latent Schr\"odinger Bridge framework for single-cell perturbation response prediction. A response-anchored autoencoder constructs a compact cellular representation that preserves dominant transcriptional response directions identified from training perturbations while encoding complementary cellular variation. In this latent space, PerturbBridge models conditional stochastic transport through a tractable approximation to the Schr\"odinger Bridge. We introduce the Perturbation-Induced Bridge Transformer, which uses perturbation and time-dependent slots to guide interactions among latent coordinates during drift estimation. Evaluations on Norman, Sci-Plex3, and Replogle RPE1 demonstrate leading performance in differential-expression direction recovery and perturbation-effect correlation, alongside competitive gene-expression prediction accuracy. \textbf{Availability:} The source code is available at \url{https://github.com/echQoQ/PerturbBridge}, with an archived version at \url{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24272128}.

papers.title_en: ST-Dist: Distilling Spatial Transcriptomics Predictions into Interpretable Gene Axes for Distant Metastasis Prediction
papers.authors: Sandesh Pokhrel, Hamid Manoochehri, Beatrice S. Knudsen, Tolga Tasdizen
papers.evidence: 将空间转录组预测的基因表达蒸馏用于活检切片转移预测
papers.tldr: 前列腺癌远处转移难以从常规H&E切片判断，且转移征象定位不清、监督标签需随访确认。ST-Dist将空间转录组模型预测的基因表达蒸馏为线性头，把每个切片的病理基础模型特征映射到具名基因轴，再用逻辑回归预测远处转移。在497例前列腺穿刺活检上AUROC达91.37%，优于九种MIL基线，并在TCGA-COAD/KIRC上保持竞争力。该方法提供从H&E到远处转移预测的简单、准确且可解释路径。
papers.abstract_en: Distant metastasis at diagnosis determines the treatment of prostate cancer, but predicting it from routine biopsy slides is challenging as the signs of metastasis are not clearly localized and are more subtle than in standard tumor detection and subtyping tasks. Multiple instance learning (MIL) on pathology foundation-model features has become the standard approach when labeled data are abundant, but such models remain hard to interpret. Distant metastasis is further challenging, because confirming the label requires clinical follow-up beyond the routine H&E slides. To this end, we propose ST-Dist, which distills the gene expression predicted by a spatial transcriptomics (ST) model into a linear head mapping each tile's foundation-model features onto named gene axes. The slide's projections along these interpretable gene axes are then used for distant metastasis prediction with a simple logistic regression.   On 497 prostate needle biopsies (205 patients), ST-Dist reaches an AUROC of 91.37%, above nine MIL baselines. It remains competitive on the public TCGA-COAD and TCGA-KIRC cohorts, and it has the highest mean AUROC over the three cohorts. The ablations on the prostate biopsies show that the gene axes outperform a linear probe on encoder features, dimension-matched principal components, random gene panels and the ST model's own predicted expression, and the gain over the probe holds on all 13 pathology encoder settings that we tested. ST-Dist thus offers a simple, accurate and interpretable route from H&E to distant metastasis prediction.

papers.evidence: 评测从组织学图像预测空间蛋白表达的H&E到mIF生成模型
papers.tldr: H&E-to-mIF生成模型常以像素级染色保真度评价，但难以反映下游临床价值。本文提出HEmIF-Bench，在八个数据集上冻结评估五个生成器，并解耦编码器特征与生成输出同UNI2比较。结果显示基础模型MIPHEI-ViT领先，但内部特征通常优于生成输出，且均未稳定超越UNI2。该基准强调染色保真不等于下游效用，为追踪生成模型何时超越纯H&E基础模型提供统一标尺。
papers.abstract_en: Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-to-multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) generators predict spatial protein expression from routine histology, yet pixel-level marker reconstruction does not establish downstream utility. We present HEmIF-Bench, evaluating five frozen generators across eight datasets spanning molecular, cellular, tissue, and patient scales. HEmIF-Bench decouples internal encoder features from generated outputs, benchmarking both against the pathology foundation reference UNI2. Mirroring the clinical workflow where pathologists rely on mIF to define cell phenotypes, delineate tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) and germinal centers (GCs), and stratify patient risk, we evaluate external CD3 recovery, single-cell classification, dense nuclear segmentation, TLS/GC segmentation, and patient survival prediction. Across the benchmark, foundation-model-based MIPHEI-ViT leads among the generators, while non-foundation models show task-specific strengths. Comparing the two routes reveals that internal encoder features generally outperform generated outputs, and larger output marker panels do not guarantee stronger downstream utility across datasets. Moreover, neither internal encoder features nor generated outputs consistently surpass frozen UNI2. These findings show that pixel-level stain fidelity does not equate to downstream utility, and that generators trained at current paired-data scales have yet to surpass large-scale pure-H&E foundation models. With the expansion of paired translation cohorts and the advancement of foundation-based generative architectures, HEmIF-Bench establishes a definitive benchmark for tracking when H&E-to-mIF generation crosses the threshold to deliver genuine value beyond routine histology for tumor microenvironment analysis and precision oncology.

papers.title_en: MELD: Mutation Effect Learning through Differential embeddings
papers.authors: Alajji, A., Jashil, R., Mall, R., Elshrif, M.
papers.evidence: 通过野生型与突变型差分预测单核苷酸变异的功能后果
papers.tldr: 单核苷酸变异效应预测对临床基因组学重要，但现有序列到功能模型依赖绝对基因组轨迹，变异评分多在训练后通过计算机诱变完成。MELD将野生型与突变体logit差Δz直接放入监督目标，结合共享CNN-Transformer编码器、突变掩码增强、多尺度突变中心池化和自适应放大因子。在ClinVar上仅1.9M参数即达AUROC 0.986，显著优于同数据同骨干的ISM基线0.800，并在共享基准上超过更大规模基础模型。结果表明直接差分监督是一种紧凑、数据高效的事后ISM替代方案。
papers.abstract_en: We introduce MELD (Mutation Effect Learning through Differential Embeddings), a compact model for predicting the functional consequences of single nucleotide variants (SNVs) by training directly on the wild-type (WT) versus mutant differential. Interpreting SNVs is central to clinical genomics, yet experimental characterization cannot scale to millions of observed variants. Leading sequence-to-function models (Enformer, Borzoi, AlphaGenome) are trained on absolute genomic tracks and score variants post hoc through in-silico mutagenesis (ISM), so the WT-mutant difference never enters the training loss. MELD instead places the logit difference {Delta}z = zmut - zwt inside the supervised objective. It combines a shared CNN-Transformer encoder, a mutant-specific mutation-mask boost, multiscale mutation-centered pooling, and a learned adaptive amplification factor . On ClinVar (1.57M variants), MELD (1.9M parameters) reached an AUROC of 0.986 versus 0.800 for a same-data, same-backbone ISM baseline, with ablations confirming the contribution of each component. On a shared benchmark, it outperformed frozen foundation models with 3-1,300x more parameters (AUROC 0.967 vs. 0.924 for AlphaGenome and 0.936 for Nucleotide Transformer). With only 50, 000 training variants, it exceeded the ISM baseline trained on all 1.48M (AUROC 0.903 vs. 0.796) variants. On BRCA1 saturation genome editing, frozen MELD achieved a Spearman {rho} of 0.42, above Borzoi (0.40), and ClinVar transfer raised it to 0.45. These results demonstrate that direct differential supervision is a compact, data-efficient alternative to post-hoc ISM scoring with substantially larger pretrained models.
